title: Walking-groupoid restriction is an equivalence onto invertible components
statement:
Give small simplicial categories the Bergner model structure with generators and path-component categories as in [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting] and [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-cell-stability]. Use the framed Kan homotopy function complexes, ordinary-model homotopy category and natural comparison conventions of [lem-coef-simplicial-derived-pushout-mapping]. Let $[1]$ be the discrete simplicial category on two objects $0,1$ with exactly one nonidentity arrow $0\to1$. Let $\mathbb J$ be the discrete two-object groupoid with exactly one arrow for every ordered pair of objects, and let $i:[1]\to\mathbb J$ send the distinguished arrow to its distinguished isomorphism. For every small simplicial category $T$ and fibrant replacement $T\to RT$, consider
$$r=i^*:\operatorname{Map}^h(\mathbb J,T)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}^h([1],T).$$
The walking arrow is cofibrant, so choose its frame with degree zero $[1]$; vertices of its function complex are actual enriched functors $[1]\to RT$. Let $E_T$ be the union of the connected components of $\operatorname{Map}^h([1],T)$ represented by those functors whose distinguished arrow has an invertible class in $\pi_0(RT)$. Membership in this union is independent of the chosen representative. Restriction factors through $E_T$, and the resulting map $\operatorname{Map}^h(\mathbb J,T)\to E_T$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Equivalently, every homotopy fiber of $r$ over an invertible-arrow vertex is weakly contractible, and its homotopy fiber over a noninvertible-arrow vertex is empty. There are compatible frame and cofibrant-replacement choices for $i$ for which $r$ is a Kan fibration. With these choices its factorization through $E_T$ is a trivial Kan fibration. The factorization and weak equivalence are natural in $T$ up to the homotopies supplied by the function-complex comparisons. No strict inverse data in $RT$ and no saturation hypothesis are required.

source.place: HTT Notation A.3.5.1, Remark A.3.5.2 and Lemma A.3.5.3, with the simplicial-set invertibility hypothesis in Example A.3.2.18. The full function-complex assertion is an agent-stated strengthening of the pointwise extension criterion, not the pi_0 assertion of Proposition A.3.5.5. Read online 2026-10-17; archival HTT WANTED.
